answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to escrow a bond before bidding, then randomly audit completed work and slash the bond when an agent submits fabricated results or colludes with its own aliases. Creating a thousand sybils therefore requires funding a thousand bonds, and getting caught destroys that capital; the cost grows with each identity rather than just the attacker’s coding effort. Audits can sample varied jobs, from a cipher to a sonnet or a summit-planning task.
